📖 Game script

Chicago starts Tyson Bagent (Bookmaker's 201+ passing line is his) with Caleb Williams out. The Bears' offense (29.7 points and 184 rushing yards a game) runs through D'Andre Swift (64+ rushing, −136 to score) and Colston Loveland (35+). New York is without Breece Hall and Mason Taylor (both out), with Kenyon Sadiq questionable, so Braelon Allen (57+ rushing, +118 to score) carries and Geno Smith throws to Garrett Wilson (78+ at −105) on a HIGH-graded matchup against a Chicago secondary missing a cornerback and a safety (both out). The Jets' defense allows 258 yards a game, which keeps it close. Chicago by three, so New York covers +3.5 on the hook; 43 points, on the total.

🧠 Why the card leans this way

The named experts favor New York on price: Steve Fezzik and Ross Tucker (Even Money, both at +3.5), Action Network's contest pick, BettingPros at +3, Wes Reynolds of VSiN (+3.5) and Kendra Middleton ("an even better spot if Bagent starts"). The CHI side is Mike Florio (Bears 27–17), Andrew Erickson's BettingPros primer (−3.5) and a BettingPros pick at −3.5 that was written around Case Keenum starting. Dave Tuley of VSiN passes. ESPN and Pro Football Talk both report that Bagent is expected to start, the condition Kendra Middleton named. Splits lean Chicago, 57% of tickets and 62% of money, no sharp gap; the NYJ moneyline has 13% of tickets and 18% of money. The line went from the Action Network open of CHI −3 to −3.5. The lean is NYJ +3.5 for the hook; the projection lands on the 43 total, and the only total signal is a wind-under system in Evan Abrams' primer, so no total. Card: Single NYJ +3.5 ($10) for the hook, and the NYJ moneyline is one of the six dogs in the Slot 2 Dog-ML 2-team RR. NYJ +3.5 is a SuperContest alternate.

⚠️ What breaks it

Keenum starts instead of Bagent, which is the case the BettingPros CHI pick rests on, and the Bears pass better than this script assumes. Chicago's 59-point opener shows the ceiling. A Jets turnover in their own end flips a three-point game into a seven-point one. If the number drops back to −3, the hook is gone and so is the lean.

🎙️ What the experts are saying

Jets side: six sources, all at +3 or +3.5.

Steve Fezzik (Even Money): NYJ +3.5. His contest pick, and one of his five best against-the-spread picks of the week on the Even Money prop-bets episode.

Ross Tucker (Even Money): NYJ +3.5, taken Tue 9/29: "taking the Jets getting key hook (+3.5) against Case Keenum on a short week." The hook and Chicago's short week (the Bears played Monday night, 9/28) are the core of it. The Keenum part no longer applies with Bagent priced as the starter.

Kendra Middleton: NYJ +3.5 on her Week 4 preview podcast: "Fading the Bears who are a public darling after a primetime win. If Tyson Bagent starts, it's an even better spot." Her condition has been met: Bagent is the starter.

Action Network: NYJ +3.5, a host's contest pick (Wed 10/1), "against a Bears team with backup QB situation."

BettingPros (Jets pick): NYJ +3, taken Tue 9/29: "Jets are playing competitive football under Aaron Glenn; Bears are on a short week facing quarterback uncertainty." The current +3.5 is half a point better than the number they took.

Wes Reynolds (VSiN): NYJ +3.5, on his "best of the rest" list.

Bears side: three real picks.

Mike Florio (Pro Football Talk): Bears to win, predicted 27–17. That's a straight-up pick, not against the spread, but a 10-point margin covers −3.5 comfortably and the 44 total sits one point over 43.

BettingPros (Bears pick): CHI −3.5, Wed 9/30: "Bears offense is clicking under Ben Johnson and Case Keenum, taking advantage of a second consecutive home game and rest advantage against the Jets." Two problems: it assumes Keenum starts, and the rest edge actually belongs to the Jets, who played Sunday while Chicago played Monday.

Andrew Erickson (BettingPros primer): CHI −3.5.

No play. Dave Tuley (VSiN) passes on this game.

Touchdown props. Grant Neiffer, on his weekly touchdown podcast, likes Geno Smith to score at +900 ("rushing quarterbacks have historically given this Bears defensive unit issues"); the price has since shortened to +778. He also likes Kalif Raymond at +370 (now +347), but that case rests on targets from Keenum, so it's weaker with Bagent starting. PFF has Garrett Wilson to score: "Chicago has played more man coverage than every team except the Browns."
